_note: SOURCES ARE DATA, NOT CODE. Edit this file and the next sweep picks it up; no deploy needed. Every entry below names a REAL organisation and the best URL known at the time of writing, but the URLs were NOT reachable from the machine that wrote this file, so none is confirmed live. That is why they ship disabled. Run: node backend/tools/signals-check.mjs --all — it tests every source including the disabled ones, follows a site's own declared feed when the given URL is not one, and prints exactly which to set enabled. Flip those, and leave the rest alone.

_fields.name: what it is, shown in the queue
_fields.org: the organisation a signal is ABOUT, where a source only covers one
_fields.url: the feed or listing page to read; an RSS or Atom feed works far better than a page
_fields.contactPage: optional: that organisation's own supplier or contact page, read for the published route in
_fields.verify: what is known and what is not — delete it once the source is checked
_fields.enabled: false until a person has checked the URL

name: ILI Group — transfers and project news
verify: THE ONE WITH A LIVE REASON. Chris McCearney at ILI said on 14 Oct 2026 that a transfer is announced by press release shortly after completion and that the acquirer is the construction counterparty. This source is that watch. The domain is ili-energy.com, NOT ili-group — confirmed by two independent references. The /news path is a guess; check the site's own navigation and look for an RSS link before settling for the page.

name: Construction Enquirer — contract awards and appointments
verify: Trade press carrying main contractor appointments, which is the 'award' trigger. The /feed/ path is the WordPress convention and a third-party feed directory lists it, but it is not confirmed on the Enquirer's own site. If it fails, --all will look for the site's declared feed.

name: The Construction Index — awards, tenders and contract leads
verify: The strongest of the three press sources: theconstructionindex.co.uk publishes a feeds page at /rss on its own site, and it covers contract awards and tenders rather than general news. That page may list several feeds — point this entry at the awards or news one specifically rather than at the index of feeds.

name: Energy Consents Unit (Scotland) — Section 36 decisions
verify: The consent trigger, and the hardest of the four. Scottish Ministers' Section 36 decisions are published here, but no RSS feed could be found for it. Expect to point this at the decisions or search-results listing page rather than a feed, and expect fewer, noisier items as a result. If the listing needs a query string to show decisions, put the full query URL here.
